about: The meaning check's test set (lib/learning/judge.ts). Each case is one lesson line with the passages it rests on and the verdict a careful reader gives. scripts/eval-judge.mjs sends them to the real judge (it costs 20b tokens; it is not part of npm test). 'layer' says which check is meant to catch a NO: 'judge' (the AI call) or 'code' (a free rule in lib/learning, unit-tested in scripts/test-learning.mjs). A 'code' case is still sent to the judge, to show whether the judge would also catch it.

passages.text: The interpreter acts as a simple calculator: you can type an expression into it and it will write the value.
Expression syntax is straightforward: the operators +, -, * and / can be used to perform arithmetic; parentheses (()) can be used for grouping.

In interactive mode, the last printed expression is assigned to the variable _. This means that when you are using Python as a desk calculator, it is somewhat easier to continue calculations, for example:
A variable can later point at a different value — even one of a different type.

cases.sentence: A variable is a value that can never change once it is set.
The equal sign gives the name width the value 20.
Python multiplies width by height and stores the result in a new variable.
cases.why: the code shows the result; nothing stores it
